title: Top Cost Drivers: heuristics brainstorm (Usage Insights)
content:
Context
- Goal: provide “Top cost drivers” + “What changed?” in Console → Usage/Cost → Insights.
- Primary audience: engineering leads + finops-ish folks trying to answer “why did spend go up?” and “what can we do about it?”
- Scope: heuristics + explainability strings (not automated actions). Must be robust enough for beta.

Non-goals
- Not a full root-cause engine.
- Not a ranking of “bad behavior” or “quality.”
- Not a place to surface customer-specific dimensions beyond fixed set.

Definitions (so we don’t fight in UI copy)
- Unit: route + model (optionally workspace/project/env/region/deployment mode filters).
- “Spend” = billed cost proxy that reconciles to billing totals (with known tolerances).
- “Tokens in/out” are billable drivers; cache hits reduce compute but may still be billed depending on plan (we need copy that doesn’t over-promise savings).
- “Retry” = additional attempt that results in additional token usage/cost; must align with billing semantics (see correctness thread).
- “Fallback” = request served by a different model/version than originally targeted due to policy/capacity; may have different unit price.

Heuristics we can ship first (candidate signals)

A) Token-out increase (dominant in most stories)
- Heuristic: detect routes where token_out increased significantly vs previous period.
- Inputs:
  - token_out_total, token_out_per_request (p50/p95), request_count
  - split by route+model
- Explanation templates:
  - “Output tokens increased +35% (from 120M → 162M) while request volume was flat (+2%). This typically indicates longer responses or changed prompts.”
  - “Output tokens per request increased (p50 420 → 610).”
- Guardrails:
  - Only show if absolute delta exceeds threshold (e.g., +$100 or +2% of total spend in selected scope) AND percent delta > X.
  - Distinguish between volume-driven vs per-request-driven.
  - Avoid blaming model if route mix changed (see Mix shift heuristic).

B) Token-in / context length creep
- Heuristic: token_in increased (especially p95) driving cost + latency; also correlates with cache miss rate issues.
- Inputs:
  - token_in_total, token_in_per_request (p50/p95), context_length histogram buckets
- Explanation templates:
  - “Input tokens increased +28% and long-context requests (>16k) doubled. Long contexts are more expensive and can reduce effective batching.”
- Guardrails:
  - If token_out moved similarly, call out that both grew (don’t over-index on context).
  - If “structured output/tool calls” are enabled for the route, mention as possible contributor (but don’t assert).

C) Request volume spike
- Heuristic: request_count increased significantly; tokens/request stable.
- Explanation templates:
  - “Requests increased +48% (1.2M → 1.8M). Tokens per request remained stable (p50 390 → 402).”
- Guardrails:
  - Always pair with “Did unit cost change?” to avoid confusion (“spend up because more usage”).
  - Require minimum baseline volume to avoid noisy percent deltas (e.g., previous period < N requests).

D) Cache hit rate drop (prefix/KV cache)
- Heuristic: cache_hit_rate dropped and cache_miss_tokens increased; attribute incremental spend.
- Inputs:
  - cache_hit_tokens, cache_miss_tokens, cache_hit_rate, cache_savings_estimate (if we can compute)
- Explanation templates:
  - “Cache hit rate dropped from 62% → 41%, adding ~+$X in compute-equivalent cost for the same traffic.”
  - “Most misses were on prompts in the 2k–4k prefix bucket (suggests more prompt variance).”
- Guardrails (important):
  - If billing does not discount cached tokens for a given plan, avoid language like “you would have saved $X” and instead say “cache efficiency decreased; can impact compute + latency.”
  - Only show when cache metrics are complete for the selected region/deployment mode; otherwise show “insufficient cache telemetry for this slice.”
  - If cache instrumentation is missing for streaming in region R, suppress this driver (see known issue from eng-platform thread).

E) Retry rate increase / error-driven spend
- Heuristic: retries increased (absolute + percent), causing extra billable tokens.
- Inputs:
  - retry_count, retry_rate, extra_tokens_due_to_retries, error_code breakdown (if safe)
- Explanation templates:
  - “Retry rate increased from 0.8% → 3.1%, contributing ~+$X.”
  - “Most retries coincided with 5xx responses and timeouts (p95 latency increased 22%).”
- Guardrails:
  - Must align with billing definition: do we bill tokens on failed attempts? (depends). If unknown, phrase as “additional attempts observed” not “billed.”
  - Avoid surfacing specific error codes if it risks sensitive info; keep categories broad (timeout, 5xx, client abort).
  - Don’t rank retries above token-out if retry impact is small.

F) Fallback/model substitution cost
- Heuristic: increased fraction of requests served by fallback model OR model price differs materially.
- Inputs:
  - fallback_request_count, fallback_rate, served_model_id vs requested_model_id, unit_price
- Explanation templates:
  - “Fallback usage increased (2% → 11%). A higher-cost model was used more often, contributing +$X.”
- Guardrails:
  - If fallback is policy-driven (e.g., “prefer low-latency”), include neutral phrasing: “Fallback routing changed model mix.”
  - If requested_model_id is missing/unstable (aliases), suppress until model bucketing is fixed (see alias duplication support ticket pattern).

G) Model mix shift (within a route)
- Heuristic: for a single route, mix shifted from cheaper to more expensive model (or vice versa).
- Inputs:
  - spend by model within route, request_count by model, price per 1k tokens
- Explanation templates:
  - “Model mix shifted: llama-3.1-70b share increased 18% → 41% of spend for this route.”
- Guardrails:
  - Ensure totals match billing (drift tolerance) before showing financial attribution.
  - Must handle model version bucketing consistently (avoid “double-counted models”).

H) Streaming overhead / partial completions
- Heuristic: streaming enabled + increased aborted streams or many short chunks; potential inefficiency.
- Inputs:
  - stream_enabled rate, client_abort_rate, average_chunks, completion_finish_reason distribution
- Explanation templates:
  - “Streaming usage increased; client aborts rose (0.4% → 2.0%), which can increase wasted generation.”
- Guardrails:
  - Needs careful language: client abort can be desired (user navigated away). Frame as “opportunity to set max_tokens / early stopping / client handling” not “bug.”
  - Only show when we have reliable abort telemetry.

I) Latency-correlated spend (capacity/queuing)
- Heuristic: spend increased due to longer runtimes / lower throughput (esp. dedicated) even at same token volume.
- Inputs:
  - p95 latency, time-to-first-token, queueing delay, GPU-seconds (if available), batching efficiency
- Explanation templates:
  - “Latency increased (p95 1.8s → 2.6s) alongside reduced batching efficiency. This can raise per-token serving cost.”
- Guardrails:
  - Only use if we can tie to a measurable cost proxy (GPU-seconds) OR keep as “performance driver” not “cost driver.”
  - Avoid blaming customer prompts when it’s infra regression; include “Check status/incidents” link if platform-wide.

Ranking / scoring approach (rough)
- For each driver type, compute an “impact score” within the selected scope:
  - Impact ≈ max(absolute_cost_delta, absolute_tokens_delta * unit_price)
  - Confidence ≈ coverage * data_quality * sample_size
  - Final rank = Impact * Confidence (with caps)
- Output top 3 drivers per scope by default; allow “view all.”

Confidence & data quality (must be explicit somewhere)
- Each driver card should include a subtle confidence indicator (High/Medium/Low) derived from:
  - Telemetry coverage (percent of events with required fields)
  - Reconciliation drift vs billing in the selected time window
  - Sample size (requests, tokens)
  - Freshness lag (hours)

Explainability copy style guidelines (DX feedback)
- Use “route” vs “endpoint”: recommend UI says “API route” with tooltip: “Normalized path template, e.g. /v1/chat/completions.”
- Prefer neutral phrasing:
  - Good: “Output tokens increased…”
  - Avoid: “Your prompts are inefficient” / “misconfigured” / “you wasted spend” (support escalation magnet).
- Always include a “Why we think this” line with 1–2 numbers.
- Always include a “What you can do” line with links (Optimize docs), but keep it optional.

Suggested ‘What you can do’ links (non-automated)
- Token-out spike → docs: max_tokens, stop sequences, response formatting, evals for verbosity drift.
- Token-in/context creep → prompt shortening, retrieval truncation, context window policy, caching prefixes.
- Cache hit drop → enable prefix caching, normalize system prompts, reduce prompt variance, pin templates.
- Retry rate → timeouts, idempotency, backoff, raise limits, check status page.
- Fallback/mix shift → routing policy, model pinning, capacity reservations.

Guardrails to avoid misleading insights (strong opinions)
1) Don’t show $ deltas if reconciliation drift is above threshold
- If totals do not match billing within tolerance (e.g., >1–2% or >$X), show banner “Totals may be incomplete; cost deltas are estimates.” and suppress driver ranking.

2) Avoid percent deltas on tiny baselines
- If previous period spend < $50 (or tokens < threshold), either suppress or show absolute only.

3) Don’t attribute causality we can’t prove
- “Correlated with” language is safer than “caused by.”
- Never claim “cache saved you $X” unless billing explicitly discounts those tokens for that customer/plan.

4) Dimension explosion sanity
- If user filters too narrowly (e.g., single hour + single model + single region), driver cards get noisy. Provide “Not enough data” state instead of nonsense.

5) Avoid double-counting drivers
- Example: token_out increase due to retries. If retries explain majority of extra tokens, show “Retries” and annotate that token_out includes retries.
- Need a simple precedence rule:
  - If retry_contribution > 30% of token delta, surface Retry driver above Token-out driver (or merge).

6) Region / deployment mode gaps
- If route tags missing for streaming endpoints in a region (known issue), don’t show “route increased” drivers; show “Data incomplete for region X” warning.

7) Model alias/version bucketing
- If model alias duplication detected, suppress mix-shift driver and show a small “Model identifiers are being normalized” note.

Example driver cards (draft copy)

Driver: Output tokens increased
- Title: “Longer responses on /v1/chat/completions (llama-3.1-70b)”
- Evidence: “Output tokens +35% (120M → 162M). Requests +2%.”
- Note: “Tokens per request increased (p50 420 → 610).”
- Action link: “See tips to control response length →”

Driver: Cache efficiency decreased
- Title: “Cache hit rate dropped for /v1/embeddings (text-embed-3-large)”
- Evidence: “Hit rate 62% → 41%. Cache-miss tokens +18%.”
- Note: “This can increase compute and latency for the same traffic.”
- Action link: “Caching guide →”

Driver: Model mix shift
- Title: “Higher-cost model used more often on /v1/chat/completions”
- Evidence: “70B model share of tokens 18% → 41%.”
- Note: “Consider pinning a cheaper default + fallback policy.”

Open questions / risks (please resolve before we commit UI)
- Billing semantics: which tokens are billed on failures/retries? Do we ever bill partial generations?
- Cache and pricing: do customers see different billing when cached? If plan-dependent, we need plan-aware copy.
- Fallback definition: is “fallback” always recorded reliably? Does it exist for all deployment modes?
- Timezone handling: what is “previous period” exactly (rolling window vs calendar week)?
- Data freshness: how to phrase “last updated” to prevent support churn.

Next steps (proposed)
- Nadia + Logan: decide minimal reliable set of driver signals for beta (recommend A/C/E/F/G; cache/streaming behind telemetry completeness checks).
- Allison: define data quality thresholds and confidence scoring.
- Alex: review copy style + tooltip language (“route”, “model version”, “fallback”).
- Dylan/Chloe: implement driver computation contract shape for ENG-3819 (including evidence fields and suppression reasons).

Notes to self
- Keep the UI humble. The fastest way to ruin trust is confident but wrong “insights.”
- Make “suppressed due to incomplete data” visible in debug view (maybe not customer-facing) so support can explain gaps.
